# Pack-boundary exceptions: the footprint that predates the rail
#
# One line per `<sha256> <path>` pair. The digest is a denylist entry; the path
# is relative to the repository root, posix separators, a trailing slash making
# it a directory prefix. `scripts/check_pack_boundary.py` skips exactly that
# digest at exactly that path.
#
# Pairing is the whole point. A file listed here for one term is still checked
# for every other term, and the term listed here is still caught in every other
# file. So this list freezes the footprint rather than opening a hole: if the
# same vocabulary spreads to a new file, CI fails.
#
# WHAT THIS RECORDS
#
# The rail was written for the practice layer, which is clean. Two systems that
# predate it are not: the personality pillar and the healing modality library
# name established third-party frameworks in code, tests, prompts, report
# templates and web copy. That is a licensing and attribution question, not a
# tooling question, and it is Tyler's call:
#
#   - keep the names and carry proper attribution and license terms, or
#   - move that content to an external pack the way the practice layer does, or
#   - rename to generic vocabulary and describe the method without the brand.
#
# Until that call is made, this file makes the footprint exact and countable
# instead of invisible. Some paths below already name a term; those filenames
# are existing repo content, not new exposure.
#
# HOW TO SHRINK IT
#
# Delete the line once the content it covers is gone. `pytest
# tests/infrastructure/test_pack_boundary.py` fails on an entry that points at
# a missing path or that nothing matches any more, so the list cannot go stale.
#
# HOW NOT TO GROW IT
#
# A new entry is a decision to ship third-party vocabulary, so it needs the
# licensing answer first. `--freeze-exceptions` exists to record this original
# footprint, not to clear a failing build.
#
# STATUS: DRAFT, generated 2026-08-18 from the seed denylist. Awaiting Tyler.
